method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, clause-by-clause reconstruction of elementary equivalence and isomorphism, replay of the term-induction proof, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison after one documented source-correction projection. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The distinction between elementary equivalence and isomorphism, the five defining isomorphism conditions, invariance of term values and satisfaction under an isomorphism, and automorphisms preserving definable subsets.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Two structures are elementarily equivalent when they satisfy exactly the same sentences. They are isomorphic when a bijection between their domains preserves every constant, predicate and function interpretation. Isomorphism therefore implies elementary equivalence.
samples.checks: The weaker-versus-stronger contrast, first-order expressibility limitation, Löwenheim--Skolem example, sentence biconditional, injectivity, surjectivity and all three symbol-preservation clauses are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Composing an assignment with the isomorphism transports every term value and every formula's satisfaction value. The source proves the term claim by structural induction and leaves the formula claim as an exercise; for a sentence the assignments are irrelevant, yielding elementary equivalence.
samples.checks: The two simultaneous induction claims, constant and variable cases, function-term calculation, cited preservation clauses, sentence step and five-property exercise are retained. The erroneous M interpretation in the M-prime term-evaluation equation is corrected under OLFOL-026.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An automorphism is an isomorphism from a structure onto itself. Every definable subset is invariant under every automorphism of that structure.
samples.checks: The self-map condition, definability hypothesis and exact image-set equality are retained.

source_observations: OLFOL-026 records a confirmed frozen-source mismatch: the recursive evaluation of a function term in M-prime used the interpretation of f in M. The target uses M-prime, as required by the recursive definition and the following equality chain, and QA projects it back solely for source comparison.
MR-P122 directly attests स्वयंरूपता for automorphism in the official mathematics glossary.
MR-P123 directly supports प्राथमिक and the सममूल्यता/सममूल्य family in an official logic glossary; the exact model-theory compound remains source-defined.
All other formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match the frozen source exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The full phrase प्राथमिक सममूल्यता was not independently attested in a Marathi model-theory source, although both components have direct official logical support.
No TeX reader build was run for this individual unit.
